explanation: WITH GRANT OPTION can be applied when one role is granted to another role, allowing the recipient role to grant that role onward.
reasoning: Snowflake's October 2026 enhancement added delegated onward role grants for account roles and database roles. The clause is not supported for grants directly to users.

distractor_analysis.why_wrong: The release specifically says grants to users do not support WITH GRANT OPTION.
The clause does not transfer object ownership.
The clause delegates a role grant; it does not change role type.

exam_trap: Role delegation and object OWNERSHIP are separate access-control concepts.
code_example: GRANT ROLE child_role TO ROLE parent_role WITH GRANT OPTION;

sources.title: WITH GRANT OPTION for role grants

explanation: The Workday Data Cloud zero-copy integration lets Snowflake query Workday tables directly while Workday remains the system of record.
reasoning: The connector mounts the Workday catalog as a catalog-linked database. Snowflake reaches Workday on SELECT rather than requiring ETL or replicated copies for the integration.

distractor_analysis.why_wrong: The integration is explicitly designed to avoid copying the tables into Snowflake before each query.
Nightly unload/reload is the opposite of direct zero-copy access.
The mounted catalog exposes namespaces as schemas and Workday tables as tables.

exam_trap: Zero-copy integration here is direct governed access, not merely a more efficient bulk copy process.

sources.title: Zero-copy integration for Workday Data Cloud (General availability)

explanation: Enable the Cortex Agent code execution tool when an agent needs Snowflake-managed code execution during a conversation.
reasoning: The generally available tool runs code in a sandboxed isolated environment and can execute scripts for data processing, calculations, and visualizations. The agent decides when to invoke it during orchestration.

distractor_analysis.why_wrong: Search Optimization improves data lookup performance and does not execute agent-generated Python.
Replication provides continuity/data movement, not conversational code execution.
External table refresh is unrelated to executing code inside a Cortex Agent workflow.

exam_trap: This built-in code execution tool is different from search/retrieval tools and from application-hosted execution.

sources.title: Cortex Agent code execution tool (General availability)

explanation: Release 10.25 added preview support for Java 21 to the Snowpark API for Java and Scala, alongside Java 11 and Java 17.
reasoning: This is a runtime compatibility update for Snowpark Java/Scala and is time-sensitive, so the question retains Preview lifecycle metadata.

distractor_analysis.why_wrong: Java 8 was not the newly added version in the cited release.
Java 15 was not the version announced.
Java 25 was not announced in that Snowpark release note.

exam_trap: Treat runtime-version questions as freshness-sensitive; lifecycle status can change after the release date.

sources.title: 10.25 Release Notes: Java 21 support for Snowpark (Preview)

explanation: The Native Apps observability update supports event sharing for Cortex Agent telemetry, using AI_METADATA by default and AI_CONTENT after consumer approval of the relevant app specification.
reasoning: The capability gives providers observability while preserving consumer control and IP protections around what is logged and shared.

distractor_analysis.why_wrong: Fail-safe is not the mechanism for provider agent telemetry sharing.
Observability does not require transferring database ownership.
Warehouse result caching is unrelated to agent telemetry event sharing.

exam_trap: Native App telemetry sharing levels and consumer consent are governance concerns, not ordinary query-history behavior.

sources.title: Snowflake Native Apps: Observability for Cortex Agents

explanation: Cortex AI Function Evaluation is designed to compare AI function or Cortex AI configurations against labeled data while measuring quality, cost, and token usage.
reasoning: The public-preview feature creates repeatable evaluation baselines and supports comparing prompts, models, or implementations with consistent datasets and metrics, which directly supports production MLOps evaluation and governance.

distractor_analysis.why_wrong: A resource monitor is a cost control and does not perform labeled quality evaluations.
Time Travel provides historical data access, not AI quality benchmarking.
Snowpipe load history tracks ingestion, not model or prompt evaluation.

exam_trap: Evaluation and monitoring are related but distinct: this feature measures AI output quality and cost against test data.

sources.title: Cortex AI Function Evaluation for measuring quality (Public Preview)

explanation: Account posture reporting in the Trust Center aggregates scanning status, open findings, and at-risk entities and can generate a posture PDF report.
reasoning: This feature supports security monitoring and compliance review by summarizing scanner enablement, configuration changes, and violation/detection activity over a selected period.

distractor_analysis.why_wrong: Query acceleration is a performance feature, not a security posture report.
Dynamic table target lag is a pipeline freshness property.
Result cache inspection does not aggregate security findings or scanner status.

exam_trap: Trust Center posture reporting is an account-security observability feature and was still Preview at the stated date.

sources.title: Account posture reporting in the Trust Center (Preview)

explanation: Dynamic Tables became supported on Delta Direct tables, enabling Snowflake-managed declarative transformation pipelines over that source type.
reasoning: This allows an architect to incorporate Delta Direct sources into dynamic table pipelines without replacing them with a separate batch-copy architecture solely to gain declarative downstream refresh behavior.

distractor_analysis.why_wrong: Materialized external stages are not the feature announced for Delta Direct transformations.
Fail-safe is a data recovery service and not a transformation pipeline capability.
Search Optimization on stages is not the announced feature.

exam_trap: Distinguish source-table support for Dynamic Tables from ingestion and recovery features.

sources.title: 10.22 Release Notes: Dynamic Tables supported on Delta Direct tables

explanation: Snowpipe Streaming event table monitoring exposes ingestion events that can be queried with SQL for row counts, latency, row/channel errors, and channel activity.
reasoning: The monitoring enhancement supports operational dashboards and alerting for near-real-time ingestion. Collection uses event-table logging, with LOG_EVENT_LEVEL configured appropriately on the schema unless inherited settings already enable it.

distractor_analysis.why_wrong: Time Travel exposes historical table states, not streaming pipeline operational telemetry.
Replication history is not the source for Snowpipe Streaming row/channel errors.
Result cache metadata does not provide streaming ingestion events.

exam_trap: Near-real-time pipeline design includes observability, not only ingestion configuration.

explanation: Snowflake now automatically applies best-effort response caching to identical AI_COMPLETE text calls within a query, allowing cache hits to reduce latency and avoid billing for repeated inference.
reasoning: This is especially useful when large datasets contain repeated rows or prompts. No application change is required to benefit from the caching behavior described in the release.

distractor_analysis.why_wrong: Fail-safe is for data recovery and does not cache LLM inference results.
Zero-copy cloning concerns table/storage metadata, not Cortex AI inference reuse.
External table pruning improves data scans but does not reuse AI_COMPLETE outputs.

exam_trap: The release describes best-effort caching within a query; do not generalize it to a permanent global model-response cache.

sources.title: Response caching for Cortex AI Functions

explanation: INCLUDE_USERS accepts explicit user names for a per-user quota, allowing named users to be monitored even when they do not match the quota's tag scope.
reasoning: The same update also extended EXCLUDE_USERS with a USER argument. Explicit inclusion and exclusion interact with tag scope, and an explicitly excluded user remains excluded even if the user matches the relevant tags.

distractor_analysis.why_wrong: ADD_WAREHOUSE_USERS is not the documented per-user quota method.
FORCE_TAG_MATCH is not a documented quota method.
SET_ROLE_USERS is not the method used to configure quota membership.

exam_trap: Per-user quota membership can now combine tag-based scope with explicit user names.

sources.title: Include and exclude per-user quota users by name (General availability)

explanation: Semantic view materializations can pre-aggregate frequently queried dimensions and metrics and refresh them automatically based on MAX_STALENESS.
reasoning: This can improve performance for repeated analytical queries while preserving the semantic view abstraction. The release notes state that incremental refresh is supported for additive metrics.

distractor_analysis.why_wrong: Fail-safe is unrelated to semantic-view query acceleration.
Network policies govern access and do not materialize analytics results.
Stage directory tables expose file metadata rather than semantic metrics.

exam_trap: Materializing semantic content is different from materialized views; preserve the feature's Public Preview status in time-sensitive study material.

sources.title: 10.24 Release Notes: Semantic view materializations (Public preview)
